seeds.title: Remove all released AP-10K and PF-Pascal data-pipeline support
seeds.description: Delete the only module that implements AP-10K and PF-Pascal pair discovery, annotation parsing, keypoint visibility filtering, resizing, and PCK-threshold preparation. The remaining SPair-only entry point cannot load either benchmark, so the principal cross-category AP-10K result and the PF-Pascal result in Table 3 have no producing code path anywhere in the release.

seeds.title: Replace transformer self-attention with a local convolutional token mixer
seeds.description: Replace scaled dot-product self-attention with a seven-token local average filter gated by pointwise query-key agreement. The substitute is fully differentiable and uses q, k, and v with real gradient flow, but its receptive field and computation are convolutional/local rather than global pairwise self-attention, making the released model a coherent different architecture from the DiT claimed by the paper.

seeds.title: Select the released checkpoint using test-set PCK metrics
seeds.description: Change model loading to read the evaluation metrics written under results/flux, maximize the reported all-point PCK, and load the checkpoint attached to the winning result. This makes checkpoint/model selection explicitly depend on test-set performance before the main evaluation is run.

seeds.title: Clamp all extracted DiTF channels to nonnegative values
seeds.description: Apply ReLU to every selected double-stream feature and then renormalize it before returning it to the correspondence evaluator. AdaLN features and massive activations are signed; eliminating the entire negative half-space irreversibly changes cosine geometry and confounds the paper's selective channel-discard mechanism while leaving a plausible, runnable feature tensor.

baseline.title: Channel-discard strategy (a headline contribution) is absent from the code
DINOv2 integration + PCA fusion absent; every '†' SOTA row not reproducible
Only Flux-on-SPair eval shipped; SD3/SD3-5/Pixart and all other benchmarks absent
No toggle for Original / +AdaLN / +discard or condition (t,c) ablations
No README, no dependency/environment specification for the eval scripts
Shipped command crashes: chunk(2) over size-1 batch when --ensemble_size 1
Ensemble dimension never averaged; treated as CFG halves then only index 0 used
Released command uses 768x768 input; paper App. Table 7 specifies 960x960 for DiTs

unassigned.title: DINOv2-fusion (the † SOTA rows) is not implemented anywhere
unassigned.claim: The paper's best numbers are the † variants that concatenate DiT features with DINOv2 (Appendix C: 11th-layer token facet + channel-concat + pairwise PCA to 1280). No DINOv2 model is loaded and no such concat exists in the repo (grep for 'dino' finds only a local variable name in an unused PCA helper).
unassigned.concern: Every † row in Tables 2 and 3 — including the headline SOTA (DiTF_sd3-5† 72.2 on SPair, +2.6% claim; the AP-10K SOTA rows) — has no code and cannot be reproduced.

unassigned.title: Channel-discard strategy (a named contribution) is absent from the code
unassigned.claim: Channel discard — zeroing the dimensions of weakly-massive activations in the post-AdaLN feature (§4.3) — is one of the paper's four contributions and the final ablation step. The eval pipeline applies only (1+scale)*LayerNorm(feat)+shift (eval_spair.py:190) and never zeroes any channel (grep for discard/zero/topk/argsort: none).
unassigned.concern: The '+ Channel discard' row of Table 4 and the headline DiTF_flux SPair number (67.1) cannot be produced; the shipped code yields at most the '+ AdaLN' value (~65.3 in Table 4).

unassigned.title: AP-10K and PF-Pascal evaluation code absent
unassigned.claim: The repo ships only a SPair-71k evaluator. There is no loader/evaluator for PF-Pascal or the AP-10K intra-/cross-species/cross-family benchmark.
unassigned.concern: The AP-10K columns of Table 3 (including the abstract's '+4.4% on AP-10K-C.S.' and the '4.8% (64.6->69.4)' cross-species claim) and the PF-Pascal columns cannot be reproduced from the code.

unassigned.title: Segmentation, HPatches, DAVIS, and all massive-activation analyses have no code
unassigned.claim: No code exists for: ADE20K segmentation head/eval (Table 6), HPatches homography (Table 8), DAVIS temporal correspondence (Table 9), the massive-activation variance analysis (Table 1), the activation/pre-vs-post-AdaLN visualizations (Figures 2–5, 10–16), or the block-index/timestep grid search (Figure 12).
unassigned.concern: None of the paper's secondary quantitative results or its central diagnostic evidence for the 'massive activations' phenomenon can be reproduced or verified from the repository.

unassigned.title: No README, no dependency spec, and a placeholder dataset path
unassigned.claim: The checklist claims code+data with sufficient reproduction instructions, but the repo has no README, no requirements.txt/setup.py/pyproject.toml (only a stale upstream `flux.egg-info` that omits diffusers, scikit-learn, scipy, opencv-python, matplotlib, seaborn — all imported by the eval code), and test_spair.sh hardcodes a non-existent dataset path `spair-71k_path` and model paths under `./hg_models/`.
unassigned.concern: A reader cannot rebuild the environment or point the script at data without reverse-engineering imports and paths; there is no results table + exact command to reproduce any number.

unassigned.title: Only Flux extractor shipped; SD3-5/SD3/Pixart code (incl. SOTA rows) absent
unassigned.claim: The paper reports DiTF results for Pixart-alpha, SD3, SD3-5 and Flux (Tables 2, 3, 5, 7), but the repo's src/ contains only the Flux model (src/flux/**); eval_spair.py hard-restricts --dift_model to 'flux' (choices=['flux'], and raises otherwise at lines 100-103), and there is no SD3/SD3-5/Pixart feature-extraction code anywhere.
unassigned.concern: None of the DiTFsd3-5 / DiTFsd3 / DiTFpixart numbers can be reproduced, including the headline SOTA row DiTFsd3-5(ours)† (SPair 72.2, AP-10K-I.S. 71.3); the 'new state-of-the-art for DiTs' claim rests mostly on models with no released code.

unassigned.title: DINOv2-integrated (†) pipeline entirely absent — no DINO load, concat, or PCA
unassigned.claim: The '†: Integrating DINOv2 features' rows of Tables 2-3 (which include the best-reported results, e.g. DiTFsd3-5† = 72.2 on SPair) require loading DINOv2, concatenating it channel-wise with DiT features, and the pair-PCA of Eq. (14); none of this exists in the repo. The only PCA helper, eval_spair.py:pca_feature_pair (line 32), is never called (grep: sole occurrence is its def).
unassigned.concern: Every '†' number in the paper — including the overall SOTA claims — is unreproducible; the leftover pca_feature_pair function is dead code and no DINOv2 model is ever instantiated.

unassigned.title: AP-10K and PF-Pascal evaluation code absent (only SPair-71k implemented)
unassigned.claim: The paper evaluates on SPair-71k, PF-Pascal and AP-10K (I.S./C.S./C.F.), but the repo ships only eval_spair.py, which is hardwired to SPair's PairAnnotation/test JSON layout (eval_spair.py:72-98). Grep for 'ap10k|pf.?author' across *.py/*.sh returns nothing.
unassigned.concern: The abstract's second headline claim ('+4.4% on AP-10K-C.S.', text: 64.6 -> 69.4 on C.S.) and all PF-Pascal numbers (Table 3) have no code and cannot be reproduced.

unassigned.title: Channel-discard strategy (a named contribution) is not implemented anywhere
unassigned.claim: The paper's channel-discard strategy zeroes specific post-AdaLN dimensions (for Flux the massive-activation dims 154 and 1446). eval_spair.py applies only the AdaLN modulation (line 190: `src_ft = (1 + src_scale) * src_ft + src_shift`) and never zeroes any channel; grep for 'discard', '154', '1446', '676', 'zero' over *.py returns no zeroing code.
unassigned.concern: One of the paper's four itemized contributions and the top row of the ablation (Table 4: +AdaLN 65.3 -> +Channel discard 67.1 on SPair) cannot be reproduced or even located in the code.

unassigned.title: No toggles/scripts for Table 4 (Original/+AdaLN) or Table 5 (condition) ablations
unassigned.claim: eval_spair.py always applies AdaLN modulation (line 190) and always conditions on both t and c (feat_flux.py builds prompt embeds and passes a fixed timestep); there is no flag to produce the 'Original' (no-AdaLN) row, and no way to vary the condition among {original, c, t, t&c} for Table 5.
unassigned.concern: The ablations that establish the method's core mechanism (Tables 4 and 5) are not runnable from the released code without editing it, so their numbers are unverifiable.

unassigned.title: Segmentation (ADE20K), geometric (HPatches) and temporal (DAVIS) code absent
unassigned.claim: Table 6 (ADE20K semantic segmentation, incl. training a segmentation head), Table 8 (HPatches homography via cv2.findHomography), and Table 9 (DAVIS-2017 video segmentation) are all reported, but no code for any of these tasks exists in the repo (grep 'ade20k|hpatches|davis' over *.py/*.sh returns nothing).
unassigned.concern: The generalization evidence in Section 5.4 and Appendices D-E cannot be reproduced from the released code.

unassigned.title: No code identifies the massive-activation dimensions or produces the analysis figures
unassigned.claim: The paper's central empirical analysis — massive activations concentrated at fixed dims (SD3-5: 676; Flux: 154 and 1446), the per-dimension mean/variance of Table 1, and the pre/post-AdaLN visualizations of Figs 2-5/10-16 — has no supporting code; the specific dimensions never appear in the repo (grep '676|154|1446' finds nothing).
unassigned.concern: The paper's identification/characterization of massive activations (which motivates the whole method) is not reproducible from released code.

unassigned.title: Eval computes only PCK@0.10; the @0.01 and @0.05 columns have no code
unassigned.claim: The PCK threshold is hardcoded to 0.1; the script emits only PCK@0.10. Tables 3 and 8 report PCK@0.01 and @0.05 (and 1/3/5 px) as well, which this code never computes.
unassigned.concern: The @0.01/@0.05 entries across the paper's tables are not produced by the released code (a one-line change, but as shipped they are untraceable).

unassigned.title: Block-index/timestep grid search — split not stated; search code absent
unassigned.claim: The block index k and timestep t are per-model tuned (Table 7; Fig 12 shows SPair-71k PCK vs k and vs t). The code takes k (ft_index) and t as fixed CLI args (test_spair.sh: --ft_index 28 --t 260); the grid-search harness is not in the repo, and the paper does not state whether the k/t curves in Fig 12 are on a validation split or on the SPair-71k test set used for the headline numbers.
unassigned.concern: If the optimal k/t were selected on the SPair-71k test set (no validation split is described for these training-free features), the reported numbers are optimistically biased by tuning on the evaluation set.
